notes: First docs-devex verdict (no earlier file). I followed the README on a fresh git clone of 7fbb9e1: npm ci, build and typecheck all passed. npm test FAILS test/report.test.ts:270 ('site.css must contain reportTokens() verbatim'). The repo has no .gitattributes, so Git for Windows (autocrlf=true) checks site.css out with CRLF. qa:dry in that clone fails the critical report-tests check, caps visual at 3 and gives 8.60 against 10.00 here, so the QA bot depends on the checkout. The dev server on :3312 served /, /r, /connect, /api/mcp and the skill zip with 200, and tools/list worked; I stopped it. Strong points: a clear README opening, a 60-second demo, the connector table, the flow diagram, one command per task, actionable reproduce commands, a clean tree after the runs, no secrets. What holds it back: no live URL (YOUR-SITE at README:26), so the demo cannot be tried from GitHub. The README leaves out qa:dry, the Playwright browser install and the Node version (engines >=18 is optimistic). stdio.ts:17 falls back to a dead domain. ARCHITECTURE has drifted a little. The README says MIT, but there is no LICENSE file.
improvements: Fresh-clone break on Windows (setup on Windows and Unix; QA reproducibility). Add a root .gitattributes with '* text=auto eol=lf'. Also make test/report.test.ts:270 compare with \r\n normalised to \n. Better still, have scripts/build.mjs inject reportTokens() into site.css so the hand-kept copy in site/assets/site.css goes away. How to tell it worked: on Windows with core.autocrlf=true, run 'git clone <repo> x && cd x && npm ci && npm test' and get 0 failures, and npm run qa:dry in the clone gives the same overall as the working tree (10.00, not 8.60).

README.md:11-29 (the 60-second test). The demo says 'Open the site and click the demo report', but no site URL appears anywhere, only YOUR-SITE placeholders. Deploy and put three live links at the top: the landing page, the demo report (/r#…) and https://<real-host>/api/mcp. Fill in every YOUR-SITE. Also add a fallback line inside the demo section: 'No deploy? npm ci && npm run dev, open http://localhost:3000, click See it work'. How to tell it worked: from the GitHub README, a judge gets to the demo report in one click.

README.md:132-142 Local development (honest setup). Make 'npm run qa:dry' the first QA command, and say that 'npm run qa' counts a loop, that the bot stops after the 5th failed loop, and that deleting qa/state.json resets it. Add 'npx playwright install chromium' for the ui-* checks, and add the scripts that exist but are not documented: typecheck, dev:watch, start:stdio. State the Node version. package.json engines '>=18' and docs/QA-RUBRIC.md:79 are optimistic: under Windows npm (cmd.exe), 'node --test test/*.test.ts' depends on Node 21+ test-runner globbing, recursive fs.watch on Linux (dev.mjs --watch) needs Node 20+, and the function targets nodejs22.x. Say Node 22+. How to tell it worked: a contributor never burns a counted loop by accident, and the UI checks run on a machine without a Playwright cache.

src/mcp/stdio.ts:17 (the docs must match the code; no dead links). The fallback site https://what-if-coach.vercel.app returned DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND (checked 2026-10-17 11:48 UTC), and a local build passes an empty __WHATIF_DEFAULT_SITE__ (scripts/build.mjs, stdioDefault), so every report link from the stdio server is dead. Fall back to http://localhost:3000, or require WHATIF_SITE_URL and say so. Also document stdio in the README: 'npm run build && claude mcp add what-if -- node dist/whatif-stdio.mjs'. How to tell it worked: whatif_run_scenarios over stdio returns a report_url that opens.

Small docs drift: (a) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md tools table: whatif_rehearsal_start leaves out customer_mix, demo and currency (src/mcp/tools.ts:637-648), and ShareState leaves out rehearsal.customerMix (src/state.ts:28). (b) The layout says the server instructions are in tools.ts; they are in src/mcp/instructions.ts. (c) The SITE_URL order is wrong at runtime: http.ts siteUrlFor uses the request host before VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL. (d) package.json 'description' calls What-IF 'a Claude plugin', but ARCHITECTURE says 'No plugin packaging for now'. (e) The README says 'License: MIT', but there is no LICENSE file. (f) README Cursor uses '.cursor/mcp.json', but the Connect page uses '~/.cursor/mcp.json'. How to tell it worked: a diff of tools.ts schemas against the ARCHITECTURE table shows no missing fields, and GitHub shows the licence.

There is no CI, and the QA checks only read the working tree. That is why devex scores 10/10 automated while a fresh clone fails. Add a .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs 'npm ci && npm test && npm run build' on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest, or add a QA check that runs npm test in a 'git worktree add' of HEAD. Also reword qa/ui-check.ts:90: it assumes Chromium 'is usually already cached in %LOCALAPPDATA%\ms-playwright', which is true only on this machine. How to tell it worked: the CRLF break above turns the Windows job red before a judge ever sees it.
